issues.failure_explanation: The abstract states the results for an arbitrary invertible M-matrix A and a nonnegative b, and claims uniqueness of a nonnegative solution. The paper proves uniqueness only among solutions with ||a||_W+||x||_1<1, and only for A=(2-||a||_W)I-T_n(a) with ||b||_1<(1-||a||_W)^2. Uniqueness among all nonnegative solutions is false. For n=1, A=2-2a_0 and beta=1-a_0, and the equation has the two nonnegative roots beta±sqrt(beta^2-b) whenever 0<b<beta^2. Only the smaller root satisfies a_0+x<1. The paper's own Remark and Example L admit that general M-matrices (e.g. A=nu I+V^T, which has a double root) are not covered by the Newton and SDA analysis.

failure_location.quote: Existence and uniqueness of a nonnegative solution is proved.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract and introduction. The matrix class should be A=(2-||a||_W)I-T_n(a), or more generally (2-||M||_1)I-M with M>=0, with ||b||_1<(1-||a||_W)^2. Existence and uniqueness should be stated for the solution with ||a||_W+||x||_1<1, and the SDA claim limited to this setting.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and introduction overstate the generality of the existence, uniqueness and algorithmic results. The theorems themselves are correct only for the restricted class of A and b and for the selected solution.
issues.title: Abstract overstates scope: unique nonnegative solution and applicability for a general invertible M-matrix A
issues.why_classification: Only the wording of the scope needs to change. No proof or algorithm is affected, and the formal theorems already carry the correct hypotheses.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims that the vector equation has a solution iff mu=||(A-mu I)^{-1}b||_1 has a solution, for arbitrary solutions x. The 'only if' step writes x=(A-mu_x I)^{-1}b for an arbitrary solution x. For a general solution, mu_x=||x||_1 can be any nonnegative number, including an eigenvalue of A, and A-mu_x I is then singular. Invertibility is guaranteed only for mu in [0,beta], where the paper defines f. The inverse is therefore not justified, and the equivalence is not proved as stated.

failure_location.quote: Suppose $x$ is a solution of equation \eqref{eq:equation1}, then we have $x=(A-\mu_xI)^{-1}b$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma to solutions with ||x||_1 in [0,beta], or to mu where A-mu I is invertible. Alternatively add the hypothesis that A-mu_x I is nonsingular. Either way, mu_x<beta then gives invertibility.
issues.overall_effect: The general 'iff' is unsupported. Theorem thm:solution and the later iteration results use the lemma only for solutions with ||a||_W+||x||_1<1, where mu_x<beta and the inverse exists, so their conclusions are not affected.
issues.title: Lemma lem:mu0 equivalence asserted for all solutions without invertibility of A - mu_x I
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis restriction fixes the statement. All downstream uses already satisfy the restricted hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: The text says that in the first test case Newton iteration is worse than both SDA and RFPI in iterations and CPU time. Table 2 shows the opposite. Newton needs 6 iterations, tied with SDA and far fewer than RFPI's 45, and it has the smallest CPU time, 0.5937 s against 0.8514 s for SDA and 1.0535 s for RFPI. The stated comparison is therefore false on the paper's own data.

failure_location.quote: Newton iteration is inferior to both the SDA and the relaxed fixed-point iteration in terms of the number of iterations and CPU time.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sentence to say that Newton is the fastest in CPU time and ties with SDA in iteration count. Both are much better than RFPI in iterations, but RFPI is not best in CPU time.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation of the first numerical experiment is wrong. This also distorts the claimed contrast with the second case, where RFPI is fastest.
issues.title: Text contradicts Table 2 regarding the performance of Newton iteration
issues.why_classification: Only the descriptive sentence is wrong. The tabulated data and all theorems are unaffected, so a local textual correction suffices.
